Define an endpoint

Source: R/Endpoint.R, R/print.Endpoint.R
Endpoint.Rd

Defines a binary or time-to-event endpoint by the columns of a patient-level data frame that hold it and by the direction in which it is favorable. The definitions are used by BenefitRisk, WinStat and SimSelection; any number of endpoints can be defined.

Usage

Endpoint(
  name,
  type = c("binary", "tte"),
  var = NULL,
  time = NULL,
  event = NULL,
  censor = NULL,
  positive = NULL,
  higher.better = TRUE
)

# S3 method for class 'Endpoint'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

name

Name of the endpoint, used to refer to it in the criteria of BenefitRisk and in the priority order of WinStat.

type

"binary" or "tte" (time to event).

var

For a binary endpoint, the name of the column with the values.

time

For a time-to-event endpoint, the name of the column with the observed times.

event

For a time-to-event endpoint, the name of the column with the event indicators (1 = event, 0 = censored). Give event or censor.

censor

For a time-to-event endpoint, the name of the column with the censoring indicators (0 = event, other values = censored).

positive

For a binary endpoint, optional vector of the values of var that count as 1; other non-missing values count as 0.

higher.better

Logical: TRUE if a value of 1 (binary) or a longer time (time to event) is favorable.

x

An Endpoint object.

...

Not used.

Value

An object of class Endpoint: a list with elements name, type, var, time, event, censor, positive and higher.better.

Details

A binary endpoint is a column with values 0, 1 or NA, for example the objective response (higher.better = TRUE) or the occurrence of an adverse event (higher.better = FALSE). With positive, the column can hold any codes: the values in positive count as 1 and the other values as 0, for example positive = c("CR", "PR") for a best overall response or positive = "Y" for a flag that is "Y" or blank. Missing values (NA) are excluded from the posterior distribution in BenefitRisk and make a pair uninformative for this endpoint in WinStat.

A time-to-event endpoint is given by a column of observed times and either a column of event indicators (event: 1 for an event, 0 for censoring) or a column of censoring indicators (censor: 0 for an event, any other value for censoring, as the variable CNSR of ADaM data sets), for example overall survival or progression-free survival. With higher.better = TRUE (the usual case) longer times are favorable.

The columns are named freely, so that data with any variable names (for example ADaM data sets restructured to one row per patient) can be analyzed, and any number of endpoints can be defined.

See also

BenefitRisk, WinStat

Examples

eps <- list(
  Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "os_tte", event = "os_event"),
  Endpoint("PFS", "tte", time = "pfs_tte", event = "pfs_event"),
  Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "response"),
  Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "ae", higher.better = FALSE)
)
eps[[4]]$higher.better
#> [1] FALSE

# variables in the style of ADaM data sets
adam_eps <- list(
  Endpoint("OS", "tte", time = "OSAVAL", censor = "OSCNSR"),
  Endpoint("ORR", "binary", var = "BOR", positive = c("CR", "PR")),
  Endpoint("AE", "binary", var = "AEFL", positive = "Y", higher.better = FALSE)
)
